issues.description: Function 'dd_create_zero_state' has conflicting return-type information across artifacts. In the template implementation (dd_simulation.py, line 57) the function signature is annotated to return 'DDNode' (def dd_create_zero_state(num_qubits: int) -> DDNode:). In contrast, the problem statement (problem_statement.md, line 29) explicitly specifies that the function should return a 'DD' and the reference solution (solution_repository/dd_simulation.py, line 56) implements the function with the signature 'def dd_create_zero_state(num_qubits: int) -> DD:'. This inconsistency between 'DDNode' and 'DD' in the template vs. problem statement/solution will confuse students about which type to construct and return and may lead to incorrect implementations or type-checking errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template to match the problem statement and solution: change the function signature in template/dd_simulation.py to 'def dd_create_zero_state(num_qubits: int) -> DD:' and update the function docstring to say 'Returns: A DD corresponding to the n-qubit zero state.' Ensure imports remain (DD is already imported from .dd) and adjust any in-template type hints/comments that mention DDNode so they consistently refer to DD.
